name: Wisconsin
sources: Wis. Stat. 71.06(1r), (2)(k) and Wisconsin DOR 2025 Tax Update (revenue.wi.gov/Documents/2025-Tax-Update-Three-Slides.pdf): 2025 brackets after 2025 Act 15; head of household uses the single schedule
Wis. Stat. 71.05(22)(dp), (dt) (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov): sliding standard deduction (single 12%, head of household 22.515% then single, joint and separate 19.778%), CPI-indexed
2025 maximum standard deductions $13,560 / $25,110 / $11,930 / $17,520 (TaxAct summary of 2025 Form 1 instructions; matches the statute indexed to August 2024 CPI)
Wisconsin 2025 Form 1 instructions (revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-Form1-Inst.pdf): $700 exemption per person, extra $250 for 65+
Wis. Stat. 71.05(6)(b)9; DOR 2025 Tax Update: 70% of net long-term capital gains is taxed (30% exclusion)
provisional: Tax brackets are 2025 amounts; 2026 brackets are indexed to inflation but not yet published.

Standard deduction maximums are 2025 amounts. Phase-out start points ($19,550 single and head of household, $28,210 joint, $13,390 separate) are computed from the statute's CPI indexing, not read from the published table.

The standard deduction phase-out is fitted as a straight line to zero (single $132,550, joint $155,169, separate $73,710); this is exact for single, joint and separate filers, but head of household is approximated (tax off by up to about $150). It is measured on federal AGI instead of Wisconsin AGI after the gains exclusion.
notes: Wisconsin's itemized deduction credit and married couple credit are not included.
The retirement income subtraction for people 67 and older is not included.
